top.title: Nick Saban says 24-team College Football Playoff is ‘about the money’
top.description: Nick Saban was asked about the College Football Playoff’s planned move to 24 teams on this week’s episode of New Heights, the podcast hosted by brothers Jason and Travis Kelce. The seven-time national champion coach, now an analyst on ESPN’s College GameDay, did not need long to answer. “Too many. There’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the national championship. So, what is the reason to actually do it? He’s got it. Yeah, but what you’re giving up, which is what I hate to see, is, you know, the SEC Championship Game playing the SEC Championship Game was a big thing to our players. It was a big thing to our fans. It was a tradition, and it was a great venue. I mean, there is only two teams that can play in a national championship, but more teams can play in those kinds of championship games, and there’s a lot of pride in winning the conference championship. And we’re going to give that up to have an extra game where the 24th team is going to play the ninth-best team. I’m not a big proponent of it. I think it minimizes the importance of the season,” Saban said. Ex Alabama head coach Nick Saban. (Credits – IMAGN) Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger first reported in October that the CFP had reached a deal with ESPN to double the field starting with the 2027 season, and ESPN reported days later that the sides had a handshake agreement, though the contract has not been formally signed. Under the format Dellenger laid out , conference championship games go away, the top eight seeds get byes, and seeds 9 through 24 open with on-campus games in the second week of December. Only one spot is reserved, for the highest-ranked Group of Six champion, with the other 23 coming from the committee’s rankings. ESPN is expected to pay about $350 million more for the expanded postseason, according to Dellenger’s reporting, and after the roughly $200 million in lost conference title game revenue comes off the top, about $150 million is left for the conferences to split. Big Ten and SEC schools would each net an estimated $2.5 million to $3 million a year. “There’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the National Championship” Nick Saban is OUT on the 24 team playoff, so quit askin’ NEW EPISODE OUT NOW!!! https://t.co/aehwBp51Q7 — New Heights (@newheightshow) November 6, 2026 Does the data back Nick Saban’s 24-team argument? top.title: How the NHL is bringing the ski slopes inside Rice-Eccles Stadium
top.description: Signage for the National Hockey League’s 2027 Winter Classic is displayed before a press conference held by the Utah Mammoth and NHL at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Wednesday, Jan. 7, 2026. | Isaac Hale, Deseret News Outdoor NHL games count the same as every other contest — two points in the standings. But that’s the last thing people remember about events like the Winter Classic. NHL president of content and events Steve Mayer and his team have spent the last year devising the best possible game-day experience for fans at the New Year’s Eve game between the Utah Mammoth and the Colorado Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium. In an exclusive interview with the Deseret News, he laid out his plan. “What we’re building out is a bit of a winter wonderland,” Mayer said. “And there’s probably no better place to build that out than in Utah, given the proximity to the ski resorts. “We’re building out a ski resort on the field and in that stadium, and that’s sort of the overall look and feel for our game.” What does he mean when he says they’re building out a ski resort? He means they’re literally building an area to ski. There’s a large amount of open space between the rink and the stands, given the size disparity between a hockey rink and the football field that the stadium was built to house. The NHL is putting an actual, functioning cross-country skiing track in that space. The musician headlining the intermission show has yet to be announced, but the plan is for the artist to utilize the ski track while performing. Mayer’s team is also exploring the possibility of building either a ski lift or a mountain in the corner of the stadium, which he says is made possible because of the height of Rice-Eccles Stadium. In addition, the players will enter through a “ski chalet/cabin” and there will be a large fire pit to stay cozy. The other climate in the state of Utah will be represented in the form of red rock, just as it is in the game’s official logo . “Our goal is that when a fan not in the stadium — when a fan in New York City, in Miami, Florida, in Munich, Germany — tunes into the game, they know that we’re in Utah. ... It’s a showcase for Salt Lake City. This is our chance to show off that area to the world.” A big focus of Mayer’s team is to cultivate the perfect first impression for when walking into the stadium. The “wow” factor is an invaluable part of the experience. “Being in Utah, for us, is really exciting,” he said. “I mean, the backdrop is absolutely awesome. And that obviously is going to lead to how the field is designed and the activities that we’ll have around the game. “Our goal every one of these games is to have that fan who is in that seat when they walk into the stadium go, ‘Whoa. top.title: LaVell’s trust, confidence fueled Brandon Doman’s belief that he could win
top.description: BYU’s Brandon Doman goes head-to-head with Utah’s Arnold Parker during the Utah v. BYU game at Rice Eccles Stadium at the University of Utah on Friday, November 24, 2000. | JOHANNA WORKMAN Editor’s note: Eighth in an occasional series exploring LaVell Edwards’ legacy of leadership. No player who suited up for LaVell Edwards faced more immediate pressure to succeed than Brandon Doman. Injuries to the other quarterbacks opened the door for Doman to make his first start at BYU in the last home game for his legendary coach. Doman had dreamed of this opportunity ever since he was old enough to hold a football. He waited patiently for his moment — and it was finally here. “I had seen him put all of his effort and energy behind a quarterback before, and in that moment, I knew I had Lavell Edwards in my corner, and when he said, ‘You’re my guy,’ he was going to give me every shot,” Doman said. “So, I walked out of his office with the utmost confidence that he believed in me, and that I could go lead the football team. I don’t know that there’s any quarterback that played at BYU that’s walked out of his office, having been told, ‘You’re my guy,’ who didn’t feel that way.” Adding to the pressure of the moment, which included a pesky New Mexico team, was the fact that at 4-6, BYU was on the cusp of sending Edwards into retirement with his first losing season since 1972 — four years before his new quarterback was born. Doman needed to go 2-0 to keep that from happening. In addition, Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, stopped by the locker room to give the team a pregame pep talk that included his famous line: “Don’t muff it!” “I think when that moment occurred, the prophet was there, who I loved, President Hinckley, and Lavell Edwards. I mean, I can’t think of two more iconic people in the year 2000 for a member of the church than those two, and there we were, standing and surrounding them, shoulder to shoulder, and in kind of a sacred moment with the prophet, and also this, you know, war cry to go out and play the greatest game of all time. “I felt both the spirit and the power of calmness that it brought. I also felt like I was ready to go,” he continued. “And I’ve said this my whole life, because I was raised this way, and it’s a sacred thing to me, and I don’t know what other words to use for it, but I know it’s real and it draws emotion out of me — if your mind can conceive it and your heart can believe it, you can achieve it.” Bolstered by Edwards’ unyielding support, Doman marched the Cougars up and down the field. He led the team with 349 yards passing and 51 yards rushing, including an 8-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. BYU dominated the Lobos 37-13 and sent Edwards out of his final home game as a winner. top.title: Keenan, Baird and Beirne reflect on win over Argentina
top.description: Keenan was named player of the match after his hat-trick [Getty Images] Ireland started the home leg of the Nations Championship with a comfortable 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin. Player of the match Hugo Keenan , who scored a hat-trick of tries in his first home Test in nearly two years, spoke after the game. On his return after injury: "It's been 21 months since I've been here in green and it's been tough watching on. A bit like the rest of the lads, just delighted to be out there." On his favourite try of the three: "It was at the end of three good plays, they were walk-ins. We got a bonus point playing against a really tough Argentina side. To beat them by 30 points and not play to our full potential is exciting because there is a lot to work on and get better at." Ryan Baird , who featured for Ireland for the first time in 12 months, described his pride at playing international rugby after an injury-plagued spell. "I had a few tears walking out of the tunnel before the anthems, how tough the journey was to get back here, just to soak it all in. I had the self-belief I would get back. Nothing is ever guaranteed, but it was something I had my eye on and it meant a lot." On Ireland's performance: "I think it shows us we're good enough, but we have to do it consistently. They're a great team and pushed us to the end, but I think we have a bit more in us to keep that edge until the end." nigeria.title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
nigeria.description: Hundreds of youths in Ebonyi State have staged a peaceful march through Abakaliki, the state capital, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said they came from the 13 local government areas of the state to demand a peaceful political atmosphere in which all citizens can participate without fear. The demonstrators marched through major streets in Abakaliki, displaying placards with messages including, “Democracy Needs Peaceful Ideas, Not Weapons” and “Protect Freedom of Speech in Ebonyi.” Addressing journalists during the rally, a spokesperson for the group said the youths would not accept any attempt to undermine their constitutional rights. “Our constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly are not negotiable,” the spokesperson said. The group also expressed concern over reported incidents of physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation targeting opposition figures in parts of the state. “We will not sit by while political thuggery and intimidation threaten to ruin our state’s democratic process. Every citizen, regardless of party alignment, deserves to participate without fear for their safety,” the spokesperson added. The protesters called on security agencies and state institutions to intervene and ensure a level playing field for all political parties. Another youth coordinator said opposition parties should be able to campaign, present their programmes and engage voters without threats or intimidation. “Opposition parties must be allowed to campaign safely, present their platforms, and engage with voters without constant threat of violence,” the coordinator said. The group said the march was part of efforts by young people in the state to demand accountability and promote peaceful political participation as the 2027 general elections approach. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.” Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. “Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said. “The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.” Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. Trump announced that Wiles would move to the “Trump Political Operation”, praising her for what he described as an outstanding performance as chief of staff. He remained firmly behind Trump following his defeat in the 2020 presidential election and returned with him to the White House last year. Wiles submitted her resignation to Trump on Thursday night, according to a US official who spoke to CBS News, the BBC’s media partner. Wiles, 69, was regarded as one of the most influential figures in the Trump administration and a close confidante of the president. As recently as last month, Trump dismissed suggestions that she could soon leave her position, declaring that there was “zero chance” of her replacement. “Susie is here and she’s gonna be here for a long time,” he had said. nigeria.description: Troops of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, have arrested a suspected notorious terrorist in the Kagarko Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The troops also intensified clearance operations against terrorists and dismantled several hideouts in Zamfara, as part of efforts to rid the region of criminal elements. The Acting Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Capt. Tamuno Sinivie, disclosed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna on Friday. Sinivie said troops of Sector 1, in collaboration with operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), arrested the suspect, identified as Auta Maikyala, during an intelligence-led operation on Nov. 5. He said the suspect was apprehended at a hospital in Kagarko town, where he had reportedly gone for medical attention over a gunshot wound sustained during an encounter with a rival faction. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect was allegedly involved in several attacks on communities, kidnapping, and cattle rustling. He added that the suspect was currently in custody for further investigation and prosecution. Sinivie further said that troops conducted clearance operations at Aljummu Hausa, Aljummu Fulani, and Tunga Magaji villages in the Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara on the same day. The acting media information officer said the operations led to the clearance of several terrorist hideouts, thereby restricting the activities of criminal elements and enhancing security in the affected communities. He also disclosed that the air component of the Nigerian Air Force conducted air interdiction operations against identified terrorist locations in Babban Doka and Kuyumbana Forest in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara. Sinivie said the locations were suspected to be associated with a wanted terrorist kingpin, Dogo Gide. Ibe, who described Keyamo’s position as an attempt to undermine Nigerians’ democratic rights, said excluding a major political challenger would erode public confidence in the electoral process. He stated this in a Facebook post while reacting to Keyamo’s comments on the possibility of Atiku not participating in the 2027 presidential election. Ibe argued that the exclusion of a major challenger should not be treated as inconsequential, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to decide their preferred presidential candidate through the ballot. “When a ruling party treats the exclusion of a major challenger as inconsequential, it is asking Nigerians to accept that their choice is inconsequential too. That is how you erode public faith in democracy,” he said. Challenging Keyamo, Ibe asked why the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would welcome the prospect of an election without Atiku if it was confident in President Bola Tinubu’s performance. He insisted that Tinubu should be allowed to defend his record before Nigerians, while Atiku should also be given the opportunity to present his case to the electorate. Ibe expressed confidence that Atiku would secure widespread support in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, saying the former vice president’s supporters were prepared to translate their support into votes. “On 16 January 2027, we intend to turn the support Nigerians have shown Atiku into votes and those votes into a mandate. If Nigerians send Tinubu packing at the ballot box, it will be political hell for an APC that has grown accustomed to taking them for granted,” he said. The former vice president’s aide also invoked an Igbo proverb to caution Keyamo and the APC against disregarding the wishes of voters. He quoted the saying, “A gwa ntị okwu, ntị anụghị, e gburu isi, e gburu ya na ntị,” which he translated to mean that when the ear refuses to heed counsel, it shares the fate of the head when it is lost. According to him, a political party that refuses to listen to voters should be prepared for their response on election day. Ibe further vowed that Atiku’s supporters would defend their right to choose their preferred candidate through all lawful means and exercise that right at the polls. nigeria.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai (retd.), has said that military force alone cannot defeat terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need to address poverty, unemployment, poor governance and other socio-economic factors fuelling insecurity. Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions. The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons. “Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. It can create the conditions for peace, but it cannot by itself build peace. “It can degrade a terrorist group; it cannot alone remove the grievances of poverty, ignorance and manipulation from which such groups recruit,” he said. Buratai emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and community participation in counter-insurgency operations, describing local communities as indispensable partners in the fight against terrorism. According to him, security agencies cannot achieve meaningful results without the confidence and cooperation of the communities they are deployed to protect. “No amount of firepower can compensate for poor intelligence. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated. He also warned that human rights violations during military operations could alienate local communities and provide terrorist organisations with propaganda materials to attract new recruits. Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms. He called for stronger counter-terrorism capacity within the Nigeria Police Force, arguing that the military should not continue to shoulder responsibilities traditionally assigned to civilian security institutions. “The military is not the police; it is not the social welfare agency; it is not the school system. nigeria.title: The Obidient Pulse: Obi Warns Against Uncertainty As Opposition Groups Face A Test Of Unity

FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Show And Availability Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: U.S. Consulate General Highlights Fashion’s Role in Expanding U.S.-Nigeria Commercial Ties During Lagos Fashion Week
entertainment.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . In attendance was also award-winning American-born actress and producer Osas Ighodaro . Guests also experienced a new fashion themed game developed by Lagos based Maliyo Games, highlighting fashion’s growing links with technology and entertainment. Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele speaking at the event hosted by the U.S. Consul General in her honor, celebrating her vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. Fashion is a major global industry, supporting jobs and commercial activity across design, retail, and related sectors including in both the United States and Nigeria. U.S. consumers spent an estimated $560 billion on clothing and footwear in 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. For Nigeria’s fashion industry, access to the American market offers a pathway to expand the reach of Nigerian designers while offering entry points into Africa for U.S. retailers and businesses. Since founding Lagos Fashion Week in 2011, Omoyemi Akerele has built the platform into one of Africa’s leading fashion showcases. Its 2025 edition featured more than 60 designers and welcomed approximately 15,000 guests. Lagos Fashion Week (LFW) has also become a bridge to the American fashion industry. Leading American singer Ciara walked the LFW runway in 2025, while Studio 189, the label co-founded by American actress Rosario Dawson , has shown collections in Lagos. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. The Buckeyes got there with a 30-18 loss to the unranked USC Trojans on Oct. 31, the first time Ohio State has taken two losses before November since 2011. Ohio State coach Ryan Day has already said Sayin’s return is “not going to be next week or next month.” “No margin right now. There was a thin margin last week; now there’s no margin. sports.title: Nick Saban says 24-team College Football Playoff is ‘about the money’
sports.description: Nick Saban was asked about the College Football Playoff’s planned move to 24 teams on this week’s episode of New Heights, the podcast hosted by brothers Jason and Travis Kelce. The seven-time national champion coach, now an analyst on ESPN’s College GameDay, did not need long to answer. “Too many. There’s not 24 teams in the country that can win the national championship. So, what is the reason to actually do it? He’s got it. Yeah, but what you’re giving up, which is what I hate to see, is, you know, the SEC Championship Game playing the SEC Championship Game was a big thing to our players. It was a big thing to our fans. It was a tradition, and it was a great venue. I mean, there is only two teams that can play in a national championship, but more teams can play in those kinds of championship games, and there’s a lot of pride in winning the conference championship. And we’re going to give that up to have an extra game where the 24th team is going to play the ninth-best team. I’m not a big proponent of it. I think it minimizes the importance of the season,” Saban said. Ex Alabama head coach Nick Saban. (Credits – IMAGN) Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger first reported in October that the CFP had reached a deal with ESPN to double the field starting with the 2027 season, and ESPN reported days later that the sides had a handshake agreement, though the contract has not been formally signed. Under the format Dellenger laid out , conference championship games go away, the top eight seeds get byes, and seeds 9 through 24 open with on-campus games in the second week of December. Only one spot is reserved, for the highest-ranked Group of Six champion, with the other 23 coming from the committee’s rankings. ESPN is expected to pay about $350 million more for the expanded postseason, according to Dellenger’s reporting, and after the roughly $200 million in lost conference title game revenue comes off the top, about $150 million is left for the conferences to split. sports.title: How the NHL is bringing the ski slopes inside Rice-Eccles Stadium
sports.description: Signage for the National Hockey League’s 2027 Winter Classic is displayed before a press conference held by the Utah Mammoth and NHL at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Wednesday, Jan. 7, 2026. | Isaac Hale, Deseret News Outdoor NHL games count the same as every other contest — two points in the standings. But that’s the last thing people remember about events like the Winter Classic. NHL president of content and events Steve Mayer and his team have spent the last year devising the best possible game-day experience for fans at the New Year’s Eve game between the Utah Mammoth and the Colorado Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium. In an exclusive interview with the Deseret News, he laid out his plan. “What we’re building out is a bit of a winter wonderland,” Mayer said. “And there’s probably no better place to build that out than in Utah, given the proximity to the ski resorts. “We’re building out a ski resort on the field and in that stadium, and that’s sort of the overall look and feel for our game.” What does he mean when he says they’re building out a ski resort? He means they’re literally building an area to ski. There’s a large amount of open space between the rink and the stands, given the size disparity between a hockey rink and the football field that the stadium was built to house. The NHL is putting an actual, functioning cross-country skiing track in that space. The musician headlining the intermission show has yet to be announced, but the plan is for the artist to utilize the ski track while performing. Mayer’s team is also exploring the possibility of building either a ski lift or a mountain in the corner of the stadium, which he says is made possible because of the height of Rice-Eccles Stadium. In addition, the players will enter through a “ski chalet/cabin” and there will be a large fire pit to stay cozy. The other climate in the state of Utah will be represented in the form of red rock, just as it is in the game’s official logo . “Our goal is that when a fan not in the stadium — when a fan in New York City, in Miami, Florida, in Munich, Germany — tunes into the game, they know that we’re in Utah. ... It’s a showcase for Salt Lake City. This is our chance to show off that area to the world.” A big focus of Mayer’s team is to cultivate the perfect first impression for when walking into the stadium. The “wow” factor is an invaluable part of the experience. “Being in Utah, for us, is really exciting,” he said. “I mean, the backdrop is absolutely awesome. And that obviously is going to lead to how the field is designed and the activities that we’ll have around the game. “Our goal every one of these games is to have that fan who is in that seat when they walk into the stadium go, ‘Whoa. Wow. Like, this is cool.’ It’s that first impression that we work really hard on.” The rest of the game-day experience should be spectacular as well. BYU game at Rice Eccles Stadium at the University of Utah on Friday, November 24, 2000. | JOHANNA WORKMAN Editor’s note: Eighth in an occasional series exploring LaVell Edwards’ legacy of leadership. No player who suited up for LaVell Edwards faced more immediate pressure to succeed than Brandon Doman. Injuries to the other quarterbacks opened the door for Doman to make his first start at BYU in the last home game for his legendary coach. Doman had dreamed of this opportunity ever since he was old enough to hold a football. He waited patiently for his moment — and it was finally here. “I had seen him put all of his effort and energy behind a quarterback before, and in that moment, I knew I had Lavell Edwards in my corner, and when he said, ‘You’re my guy,’ he was going to give me every shot,” Doman said. “So, I walked out of his office with the utmost confidence that he believed in me, and that I could go lead the football team. I don’t know that there’s any quarterback that played at BYU that’s walked out of his office, having been told, ‘You’re my guy,’ who didn’t feel that way.” Adding to the pressure of the moment, which included a pesky New Mexico team, was the fact that at 4-6, BYU was on the cusp of sending Edwards into retirement with his first losing season since 1972 — four years before his new quarterback was born. Doman needed to go 2-0 to keep that from happening. In addition, Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, stopped by the locker room to give the team a pregame pep talk that included his famous line: “Don’t muff it!” “I think when that moment occurred, the prophet was there, who I loved, President Hinckley, and Lavell Edwards. I mean, I can’t think of two more iconic people in the year 2000 for a member of the church than those two, and there we were, standing and surrounding them, shoulder to shoulder, and in kind of a sacred moment with the prophet, and also this, you know, war cry to go out and play the greatest game of all time. “I felt both the spirit and the power of calmness that it brought. I also felt like I was ready to go,” he continued. “And I’ve said this my whole life, because I was raised this way, and it’s a sacred thing to me, and I don’t know what other words to use for it, but I know it’s real and it draws emotion out of me — if your mind can conceive it and your heart can believe it, you can achieve it.” Bolstered by Edwards’ unyielding support, Doman marched the Cougars up and down the field. sports.title: Keenan, Baird and Beirne reflect on win over Argentina
sports.description: Keenan was named player of the match after his hat-trick [Getty Images] Ireland started the home leg of the Nations Championship with a comfortable 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin. Player of the match Hugo Keenan , who scored a hat-trick of tries in his first home Test in nearly two years, spoke after the game. On his return after injury: "It's been 21 months since I've been here in green and it's been tough watching on. A bit like the rest of the lads, just delighted to be out there." On his favourite try of the three: "It was at the end of three good plays, they were walk-ins. We got a bonus point playing against a really tough Argentina side. To beat them by 30 points and not play to our full potential is exciting because there is a lot to work on and get better at." Ryan Baird , who featured for Ireland for the first time in 12 months, described his pride at playing international rugby after an injury-plagued spell. "I had a few tears walking out of the tunnel before the anthems, how tough the journey was to get back here, just to soak it all in. I had the self-belief I would get back. Nothing is ever guaranteed, but it was something I had my eye on and it meant a lot." On Ireland's performance: "I think it shows us we're good enough, but we have to do it consistently. They're a great team and pushed us to the end, but I think we have a bit more in us to keep that edge until the end." Tadhg Beirne , who captained Ireland after Dan Sheehan went off injured, added: "I think we were very good in patches and some of the tries we scored were proper team tries but we'll be walking away from that game thinking we could have got a lot more out of it."

The Boston Bruins steamrolled the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-2 on Thursday night, but the convincing win came at a cost as rookie forward James Hagens exited the contest with an apparent lower-back injury. Hagens left the game early in the third period after Penguins defenseman Samuel Girard landed a cross-check to his lower back. The 20-year-old immediately appeared uncomfortable, holding his back before making his way to the bench to receive medical attention. He subsequently headed down the tunnel and did not return for the remainder of the contest. James Hagens exited tonight's game after taking this cross-check from Samuel Girard… pic.twitter.com/Bo5w3E5lc8 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — NESN (@NESN) November 6, 2026 Before his departure, Hagens had logged 11:57 of ice time across 15 shifts and recorded four shot attempts. The Bruins did not provide an update on his condition after the game. The injury is a concerning one given the impact Hagens has made during his rookie campaign. He has accumulated six goals and six assists for 12 points in 17 appearances, placing him among the NHL’s most productive first-year players. His 12 points lead all rookies, while his six goals are tied for second behind Roman Kantserov, who has scored eight. Beyond his offensive contributions, Hagens has demonstrated a willingness to contribute defensively. He has amassed 19 blocked shots, ranking fourth among rookies in that category. Five of his six goals have also come from opportunities around the net, showing his effectiveness in high-danger scoring situations. Boston has benefited from his contributions on a line alongside Casey Mittelstadt and Elias Lindholm. The trio has produced a plus-five goal differential across 13 games together, making it the Bruins’ most effective line during that stretch. Hagens was selected seventh overall by Boston in the 2025 NHL Draft and is in the second year of his three-year entry-level contract . The Bruins have two days off before hosting the Florida Panthers at TD Garden on Sunday. With Matthew Poitras also dealing with a nose injury this week , Hagens’ condition could become another concern for Boston. technology.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
technology.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. It's not surprising to me that you can get to it, but how little effort you need to put into setting that up to get models to share anything.” The researchers tested nine models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, Z.ai’s GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5.6-Luna, and GPT-6.1-Sol, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5. technology.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
technology.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. technology.title: PyTorch 2.15 tackles the 'one bad GPU' problem
technology.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. technology.title: US air traffic control enters the 21st century, starts to abandon floppy disks
technology.description: The Federal Aviation Administration still uses computers that require floppy disks. But those are finally on the way out within the next few years. Yes, it’s still 2026, and yes, you read that right: The FAA – the agency responsible for overseeing aviation safety in the US – is finally getting rid of four systems dating back to the 1980s that remain in use at more than 400 facilities around the country, the agency announced on Thursday. “Good news America: floppy disks are out, 21st century tech is in,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in the FAA’s announcement. Only a few decades late, Sean, but we’re sure the flying public appreciates it. The new system, known as Enterprise Information Display System ( E-IDS ), is designed to consolidate data from various systems into a common digital platform, allowing air traffic controllers to access operational information and alerts needed to manage flights. E-IDS is replacing four legacy systems: Information Display System 4, used to track weather and operational info; the Automated Surface Observing System Controller Equipment Information Display System, which also relays weather information; the NAS Information Display System, which relays information about airports and other airspace conditions; and the En Route Information Display System (ERIDS), which handles information about flights. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work.
